samples.question: The picture shows a sheet of white paper carrying one solid red dot and a 5 by 5 square grid of 25 dark solid triangular arrowheads, one arrowhead in every cell of the grid. Four small blue squares printed at the four corners of the grid mark its extent: each blue square sits at the outer corner of a corner cell, so the four blue squares are the corners of the square block of 25 cells. Every arrowhead is the same size and shape, and each one sits at the centre of its own cell; only the direction it points differs from cell to cell. Apply this rule to the grid: shade a cell if, and only if, that cell's arrowhead points straight at the red dot, that is, if the ray leaving the arrowhead's blunt back through its sharp tip would run into the red dot. Every other arrowhead is turned well away from the red dot, by at least 55 degrees. The shaded cells then draw one of these five symbols on the 5 by 5 grid: plus (the whole middle row and the whole middle column shaded, making an upright cross), ex (both full diagonals shaded, making a diagonal cross), tee (the whole top row plus the rest of the middle column shaded), ell (the whole left column plus the rest of the bottom row shaded), cee (the whole left column plus the rest of the top row shaded). One or two cells may be shaded wrongly; take the symbol that the shaded cells match most closely. Which symbol do the shaded cells form? Answer with one word.
